notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates. It also updates the SCCM Retro app for Horizon, on your SD card and for new downloads.

Two Joy-Con pairs: two pairs now work as two controllers, each with its own port, and in games each player's pad is their own. The port order you set stays with each pair after a restart. To pair two Joy-Cons, hold L on the left one and R on the right one at the same time. Any left and right Joy-Con pair this way, from different sets too, and a Joy-Con whose partner is gone can pair with another one. A Joy-Con that reconnects goes back to its own pair only, so two pairs never swap halves. In Wii games, each pair's motion follows its own Joy-Cons.

PS1: a game can run on PCSX ReARMed instead of SwanStation, from its Performance menu (PS1 Emulator, Emulator core). ReARMed was written for ARM chips like the Switch's and needs much less of the CPU: on our test console it held full speed at about half the CPU clock SwanStation needed. Try it for a game that drops below full speed. It draws at the original resolution only, and a few games may want a PS1 BIOS file with it. Your memory card moves across between the two; save states do not.

Standalone PPSSPP: L and R work, and RetroAchievements sign in by themselves.

MAME games that come with a disk image (.chd), such as Um Jammer Lammy NOW!, import and start, added as a folder or a zip of one.

SCCM Retro app: Remove shows its progress while it counts the SD card's SCCM-Retro folder. It could sit for minutes on "Checking the SD card and the console" with nothing on screen.

New and lightly tested: the Joy-Con changes were tested with the console's own Joy-Cons and simulated pairs, not yet with two real Bluetooth pairs. The app's Remove change has not run on a console yet.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
